title: Push notification batcher and its tests
name: Push notification batcher

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests wait for asynchronous work, one that could make them pass or fail nondeterministically? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: In "flushes a partial batch after the interval", the test sleeps for exactly 50 ms, the same as flushIntervalMs. The batcher's timer and the test's timer are due at about the same time, and even when the flush timer fires first, sendBatch runs in a chained .then and may not have recorded the batch by the time the test resumes. Under CI load the assertion sometimes sees zero batches. The test should use fake timers or await batcher.drain() / the "flushed" event instead of a wall-clock sleep.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With maxBatchSize 3, a caller enqueues 3 messages and then immediately 1 more. With no further calls, when is the 4th message sent?
choices: Together with the first three, in the same sendBatch call
Only when drain() is called; the timer was cleared by the full-batch flush
After flushIntervalMs, in its own batch, because enqueue starts a new timer once the previous one was cleared
Never, because pending was spliced to an empty array
choiceQuestions.explanation: The third enqueue calls flushNow, which clears the timer, sets it to null and empties pending. The 4th enqueue pushes to pending and, because timer is null, schedules a new setTimeout, so the message goes out alone after the interval. It can't join the first batch, which was already spliced off. drain isn't required, and the message sits in the new pending array, so it isn't lost.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What happens to later flushes if gateway.sendBatch rejects for one batch?
choices: The inFlight chain stays usable, because the rejection is handled and turned into a "flushError" event
Every later flush is skipped, because inFlight is now a rejected promise
drain() rejects with the gateway error
The batch is put back into pending and retried on the next flush
choiceQuestions.explanation: The second argument to .then handles the rejection and emits "flushError", so the promise stored in inFlight resolves and the next .then still runs. inFlight never rejects, so drain resolves normally. Nothing re-queues the failed batch.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the "flushes immediately when the batch is full" test await drain() before asserting, rather than asserting right after the three enqueue calls?
choices: Because enqueue throws if it is called after drain
Because sendBatch is invoked inside a .then callback, so it has not run yet when enqueue returns
Because the 10-second timer must be cancelled or the test process hangs
Because drain is what triggers the full-batch flush
choiceQuestions.explanation: flushNow schedules sendBatch via inFlight.then(...), which runs in a later microtask, so gateway.batches is still empty right after enqueue returns. Awaiting drain waits for the chain to finish. enqueue never throws, the full-batch flush already happened inside enqueue, and flushNow already cleared the timer, so cancelling it isn't what drain is for here.
